Estas son las noticias de España más recientes que encontré, del 5 al 18 de octubre de 2026. La búsqueda no devolvió un resumen completo de la última semana, así que es un panorama parcial.

**Política y elecciones**
- Tras la convocatoria del adelanto electoral, el PSOE aprobó un comité electoral que dirigirá la campaña, y el PP y Vox reaccionaron con fuerza. Las elecciones generales son el 29 de noviembre (29N).
- Los partidos del Frente Amplio acordaron proponer a Ada Colau como candidata a la Presidencia del Gobierno.
- Feijóo prometió una ley antiocupaciones tras el 29N, y se la encargó a Xavier García Albiol.
- Rufián y Montero harán el primer acto de precampaña en Barcelona el próximo 24 de octubre.
- Sobre el voto de los descendientes de exiliados, Vox celebró que el Supremo le diera la razón con la 'ley de nietos'.

**Vivienda y protestas**
- La manifestación por la vivienda en Barcelona reunió a 120.000 personas según los organizadores, y terminó con cargas policiales y contenedores quemados.
- En Madrid, la acampada de Sol resiste a la lluvia tras tres semanas de protesta por la vivienda.

**Meteorología**
- Sánchez pidió precaución ante la dana Adam y seguir las indicaciones de emergencias.
- Hubo aviso rojo por lluvias muy intensas en Valencia, Alicante, Ibiza y Formentera.

**Economía**
- La gran banca española ganó cerca de 29.235 millones de euros hasta septiembre, un 15 % más.
- La excepción ibérica, aprobada por la Comisión Europea, ayuda a mantener los precios de la energía eléctrica.

**Sucesos y otros**
- Ocho detenidos y tres toneladas de hachís incautados de una narcolancha en Huelva.
- Murió un hombre en Burgos al intentar salvar a su vecino que se caía por la ventana.
- En Bilbao, Pradales consideró "intolerable" reivindicar la lucha armada tras 15 años del fin de ETA.

Para seguir la actualidad al minuto, consulta las cabeceras directamente, como eldiario.es o Infobae, que publican resúmenes diarios.

Here's what the search turned up for Spain in mid-October 2026, with the most recent items first.

**Politics: snap election**
Pedro Sánchez has called a snap general election for 29 November, and the campaign is well underway. Parties are forming alliances while left-wing divisions persist, with housing a central issue. The parade took place against a tense political backdrop, after Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap general election for 29 November. Polling is mixed: one report says snap vote could bring PP, Vox to power as polls show falling support for Sanchez, while a CIS poll put the PSOE 11.8-point lead, according to SpainNews.co.uk's headline. Those two findings conflict, so treat the polling picture as unsettled. On the campaign trail, Sánchez held a PSOE rally in Madrid on 17 October, and a Olive Press piece covers a corruption-related allegation involving his wife, Begoña Gómez, which she has not been cleared of in these reports.

**Migration and Ceuta**
King Felipe VI made his first visit to Ceuta during his reign, amid an ongoing migration crisis there. Migrants have alleged mistreatment by soldiers after camps were cleared ahead of the royal visit. Sánchez has also rejected criticism of Spain's migration policy.

**Protests and labour action**
- Education protests: Police charged students at a picket line at Madrid's Complutense University during a public-education strike, and four protesters have been arrested, according to police sources.
- Madrid doctors have called 12 days of regional strikes.
- Housing: Tens of thousands marched in Madrid after an elderly woman's eviction became a symbol of the housing crisis.
- Rail: train drivers have called a strike for Wednesday, October 29, with risk of cancellations & delays on the rail network. Note that 29 October 2026 falls on a Thursday, so the date or weekday in that report may be wrong; check Renfe's notices before travelling.

**Economy**
Inflation reached 4.9% as fuel prices surge in Sept, per SpainNews.co.uk. The IMF has raises Spain's 2026 growth forecast to 2.5%. Feijóo to back Hernández de Cos for ECB presidency, and unions are pushing for a higher minimum wage in 2027.

**Weather**
Forecasters have warned of storms. Costa del Sol braces for torrential rain as AEMET issues yellow warnings ahead of weekend deluge, and a cold snap and heavy rain have been forecast for the Costa Blanca.

**Sport**
Real Madrid's Vinícius was banned for Clasico after hair-pull red card. Spain was also punished by FIFA for Islamophobic chants during Egypt friendly.

**Other**
A Malaga care home lift accident killed two residents and injured four. Benidorm was named Europe's greenest town in a Green Cities award.

King Felipe VI made his first visit to Ceuta on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, as the city deals with a long-running migration crisis. The AP coverage syndicated across several outlets reports the following.

**The visit:** The king and Queen Letizia came to show solidarity with residents and with the victims of the crisis, which has also strained relations with Morocco (index 1-1). The royal agenda describes the aim as showing the support of the Crown for Ceuta's institutions and society. The couple planned to meet local officials and visit a school, and to visit a cemetery where dozens of unidentified migrants who died in the July crossing attempts were buried (indices 3-10, 3-12, 3-13). Large crowds turned out to greet them (index 1-16).

**Background:** About 80,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta in July, and more than 140 people died trying to reach European soil (index 1-2, 1-3). Most returned quickly, but the mayor estimates up to 15,000 people remain in the city of 84,000 residents, though the exact figure is unknown (index 1-4, 1-5).

**Political and social context:** Their presence has created social tension and become a national political issue, with opposition parties hoping to use migration concerns against the government ahead of next month's elections (index 1-6). Residents say national authorities have left them feeling abandoned (index 1-14). Amnesty International has alleged mistreatment and torture by Spanish soldiers, and the government is investigating those allegations (index 1-12).

**Melilla:** The royal couple were due to travel to Melilla, Spain's other North African exclave, on Wednesday, October 14. This is the first visit by a Spanish monarch to either city since Juan Carlos I toured them in 2007 (index 1-7, 1-8).

Here are three of the biggest stories in Spain from roughly 12–19 October 2026:

1. **Snap election campaign:** The campaign for the general election on 29 November, which Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called earlier in October, is in full swing, with housing the main issue, parties forming alliances while the left stays divided, and polls disagreeing on whether the PP and Vox could win power. [The Olive Press, 18 Oct](https://theolivepress.es/spain-news/2026/10/18/spain-political-roundup-october-18)

2. **Royal visit to Ceuta and Melilla:** On 13 October King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia made the first visit by a Spanish monarch to Ceuta since 2007, where up to 15,000 people remain after a July migration crisis in which about 80,000 crossed and more than 140 died, and they went on to Melilla the next day. [ABC News / AP](https://abcnews.com/International/wireStory/spains-king-queen-visit-ceuta-territory-grapples-protracted-149)

3. **DANA Adam storm:** AEMET, Spain's weather agency, issued a special warning for torrential rain and thunderstorms along the Mediterranean coast and the Balearic Islands from Saturday 17 October, and Sánchez urged people to follow emergency instructions. [Meteovigo, 16 Oct](https://www.meteovigo.es/actualidad/dana-adam-aemet-aviso-especial-incertidumbre-16-octubre-2026.html/amp)

Other news from the week included student and doctor strikes in Madrid and a national train drivers' strike called for 29 October. The large Barcelona housing protest happened on 5 October, which is outside the 7-day window. Which stories count as "most important" is my judgment.
